message.content:
Elias stood at the apex of the world, where the sky fractured into shards of obsidian and indigo. The wind, a relentless tyrant, battered the glass panes of the lantern room, screaming as it tried to tear him from his post. For forty years, Elias had been the silent guardian of the jagged coastline, a solitary figure bound to the rhythmic pulse of the great lens. He did not mind the isolation; he cherished the clarity of duty. The beam swept across the black waters like a divine finger, piercing the fog, guiding lost souls away from the treacherous rocks.

Tonight, however, the sea was angry. A storm of unprecedented fury churned the ocean into a frothing cauldron of white foam and dark chaos. Elias adjusted the clockwork mechanism, his hands steady despite the trembling of the tower. He watched the horizon, a thin, fragile line separating the known from the void. Suddenly, a flash of light, erratic and desperate, flickered from the south. A ship, small and fragile against the mountainous waves, was drifting dangerously close to the Devil’s Teeth.

Elias’s heart hammered against his ribs. He increased the intensity of the beacon, pouring every ounce of his will into the machine
